title: Perf canary deployment: Helm chart wiring + Terraform IAM/secrets + regional rollout sequencing
creator: Noah Patel
description:
Objective
Ship deployment plumbing for perf-canary into production with safe defaults:
- Helm chart in redwood-helm-charts with environment/region config, resources, and guardrails.
- Terraform wiring for service account, least-privilege IAM, and secrets (internal inference auth + metrics write).
- Documented rollout sequencing across regions (start us-east), including safe-disable/rollback steps.

Context
perf-canary runs synthetic prompts against internal inference endpoints and emits per-model performance metrics (p95 latency, tokens/sec, breakdown signals). Deployment must:
- Stay under overhead budget (<0.5% GPU capacity per region for covered models).
- Avoid accidental wide fanout (e.g., enabling all models/regions by mistake).
- Ensure no customer data collection (no prompts from prod traffic; strict redaction).
- Integrate cleanly with SRE on-call + incident-bot routing (handled in ENG-4878), but this ticket owns the runtime infra pieces.

Scope / Deliverables
1) Helm chart (redwood-helm-charts)
- Chart name: perf-canary
- Values support:
  - region (required)
  - environment (prod/staging)
  - targetModels (explicit allowlist; no default ‘all’)
  - targetTier (hosted/dedicated; default hosted)
  - hardwareSku (optional, but if provided must be validated against allowed list)
  - qpsCap + tokenBudget/capacityBudget knobs (default conservative)
  - baselineStore config (endpoint + bucket/path, read-only creds)
  - metrics backend (Prom remote-write / internal gateway)
  - alert webhook config (off by default in prod; enabled only after warning-only bake)
  - disableSwitch (hard kill via config map; used by SRE)
- Pod security + reliability:
  - runAsNonRoot, readOnlyRootFilesystem
  - resource requests/limits pinned (CPU/mem), and explicit max concurrency
  - PDB + HPA disabled by default (canary should be predictable)
  - liveness/readiness probes that reflect ability to run loop + push metrics
- Guardrails:
  - “requireExplicitRegion=true” and “requireExplicitModelList=true” style validation in templates (helm fail if missing)
  - cap maximum number of models per deployment (default max=5; override requires manual approval in values + label)

2) Terraform (redwood-terraform)
- Service account: perf-canary-prod (and perf-canary-staging)
- Secrets:
  - internal inference auth token / mTLS material (depending on which auth path we standardize)
  - metrics write credentials (if needed)
- IAM:
  - read: baseline artifacts (object storage) scoped to perf-canary prefix
  - write: metrics endpoint (if gated by IAM)
  - NO access to customer logs/traces; no broad read permissions
- Auditability:
  - ensure changes to canary target models/regions are recorded (control plane audit handled elsewhere; here ensure infra changes show up in terraform plan/apply)

3) Rollout sequencing + operations notes
- Define default rollout plan:
  - Stage: staging-us-east → 48h bake, validate metrics present, no cardinality blowups, overhead within budget.
  - Prod Phase 1: prod-us-east (2–3 models) warning-only alerts for 1 week.
  - Expand: prod-eu-west after baselines aligned + telemetry pipeline latency confirmed.
- Rollback/safe-disable:
  - helm rollback to previous release
  - set disableSwitch=true to stop traffic generation without removing deployment
  - hard stop by scaling replicas=0 (documented as last resort)

Acceptance Criteria
- Helm chart merged and deployable in staging + prod namespaces.
- Terraform merged: SA + secrets + least-privilege bindings for staging/prod.
- Canary can be deployed per region with explicit model allowlist; chart fails closed if unspecified.
- Confirmed safe-disable procedure (documented + tested once in staging).
- Observability checks documented: where to see canary health, QPS, capacity usage, and last successful baseline fetch.

Testing / Validation
- Staging deployment:
  - verify canary loop runs and emits metrics within 5 minutes
  - verify canary respects qpsCap and capacityBudget under load
  - verify baseline fetch failures degrade gracefully (emit health=degraded + no alerts)
  - verify disableSwitch stops requests but keeps process alive (health shows disabled)
- Production dry run (no alerts):
  - deploy with alerting disabled; verify dashboards show expected series
  - confirm no sensitive logs (spot check logs for prompts/IDs)

Notes / Open Questions
- Baseline store access path: confirm final bucket + prefix naming with Nadia (baseline pipeline) to avoid cross-env contamination.
- Secret format: prefer workload identity where possible; only use static tokens if required by inference gateway.
- Region naming: align with control plane region canonical strings to avoid mismatched labels (prevents silent ‘no data’ dashboards).

Owners / Reviewers
- Owner: Vanessa Ortiz (fleet + rollout coordination)
- Reviewers:
  - Sean Gallagher (SRE readiness)
  - Logan Wright (telemetry platform requirements)
  - Rafael Mendes (on-call routing constraints / disable switch expectations)
  - Connor O'Brien (release sequencing alignment)

Rollout Checklist (for ENG-4880)
- [ ] Terraform applied in prod-us-east
- [ ] Helm deployed perf-canary in prod-us-east with 2–3 models
- [ ] Dashboards show data; metric cardinality within budget
- [ ] disableSwitch drill completed
- [ ] Warning alerts only enabled (no paging) until thresholds tuned

Also: keep labels limited (model, model_version, region, sku, runtime_build_id, kernel_id) — no prompt bucket labels in prod metrics.
